findings.issue: The selector was just stored at mem[_23] (as `mem[mem[64]]`, with _23 a copy of mem[64]) yet the revert prints it as the memory slice `mem[_23 len 4]`, so the error can't be identified; the string payload is likewise raw memory.
findings.rule: Forward stores to loads through the equality `_23 == mem[64]` (no store to 64 in between), so `mem[_23 len 4]` becomes the constant selector and the revert decodes as `revert with 0x4ff9e48a, string`.

findings.issue: The 36-byte payload is split as a 32-byte word holding the selector plus a 4-byte memory slice (the uint32 struct field, P18), instead of a 4-byte selector and one ABI word, unlike the neighbouring `revert with 0xd82f6adb, mem[_402 + 64]`.
findings.rule: Re-split a revert payload of the form `Bytes(32, sel << 224) ++ Bytes(4, x)` at byte 4 into `sel, uint32(x)`; read a 4-byte slice ending a 32-byte word as `uint32(word)`.

notes: Functions over ~300 lines (getDONs, getDON*, addDONs, updateDON, setDONFamilies, updateNodes, addNodes, getNodes*) reviewed by structure; the rest fully. All 35 source loops are shown as whiles (updateNodes' outer loop as a labeled `loop1: while True` with `continue loop1` from the inner one; _removeDON's `while (length() > 0)` as `while stor[_122]`). The other whiles are implicit: via-IR zero-initialization of `new string[](n)`/`new Struct[](n)` (`while idx < 32 * _2: mem[idx + 160] = 96` or a fresh struct per element), calldata decodes of string[]/tuple[], memory ABI encodings of the returned struct arrays and of string[] error payloads (InvalidNodeCapabilities) (P7). Storage strings are copied with copy lines. P4: the header counts 56 `concat(mem[N])`, but 67 more one-element keys use a computed address (`stor18[concat(mem[_402 + 64])]`), 123 in all. P8: `mem[0] = k; mem[32] = slot` before every mapping access (829 such lines), and dead `mem[0] = 4; mem[0] = stor4[...]`. P11: the push bounds check `if _27 >= stor6.length: revert Panic(50)` after `length++` (12). P10: the EnumerableSet.add result flag `if stor7[k]: _32 = 0 else: ... _32 = 1; if not _32: revert`. Custom errors and events print as raw selectors/topics (database). No semantic error found.
summary: Faithful via-IR text with no aborts and all 35 loops shown as whiles; readability suffers from raw sha3 slot arithmetic for EnumerableSets inside mapped structs, reverts whose selector is left as a memory slice, and many dead scratch-memory writes.
